scope: Owner-operated startup objectives for one workspace. No historical usage data or third-party telemetry is required.

prerequisites: Stop API and worker writes, then set PRIVATE_PRODUCTION_WRITES_QUIESCED=true only for the backup invocation.
Use the pinned PostgreSQL 18.4 pg_dump and pg_restore clients and a reachable S3-compatible endpoint.
Restore only into an empty isolated database and bucket, then set PRIVATE_PRODUCTION_ISOLATED_TARGET=true only for the restore invocation.
Keep database, object-storage, archive-encryption, and key material outside the archive and provide them through the OPS-001D secret boundary.
recovery.promotionRule: Promote only an exit-zero restored result with zero missing and extra objects and met RPO/RTO; otherwise discard the isolated target and retry from the last valid archive.

secrets.name: POSTGRES_APP_PASSWORD+POSTGRES_MIGRATOR_PASSWORD+POSTGRES_WORKER_PASSWORD
secrets.rotation: Change the role's secret in the deployment secret store and redeploy: the bootstrap step resets all three login passwords on every run, and migrate, API, and worker pick theirs up when they restart. Keep the four database passwords distinct.
secrets.recovery: Recover from the deployment secret store; a restore target needs all three before its bootstrap step, and no recovery archive holds them.

secrets.name: POSTGRES_PASSWORD
secrets.rotation: Create a new superuser credential, update the deployment secret, rerun the bootstrap step (the only service that uses it), then revoke the old credential after readiness succeeds.
secrets.recovery: Recover from the deployment secret store; never place the credential in a recovery archive.

secrets.name: OBJECT_STORAGE_ACCESS_KEY+OBJECT_STORAGE_SECRET_KEY
secrets.rotation: Create a second scoped storage identity, update API/worker/recovery secrets, verify file access and backup, then revoke the prior identity.
secrets.recovery: Recover the scoped identity from the deployment secret store independently of archived object bytes.

secrets.name: SMTP_USERNAME+SMTP_PASSWORD
secrets.rotation: Issue replacement SMTP credentials, update the API secret, verify one delivery, then revoke the prior credentials.
secrets.recovery: Recover from the mail-provider credential owner; application backups do not contain provider credentials.

secrets.name: AUTH_MFA_ENCRYPTION_KEYSET
secrets.rotation: Add a new active key while retaining prior decrypt keys, restart API, verify MFA, then retire old keys only after dependent rows have been re-encrypted or expired.
secrets.recovery: Recover the complete versioned keyset from the deployment secret store before restoring encrypted MFA data.

secrets.name: AUTH_THROTTLE_SUBJECT_KEYSET
secrets.rotation: Add a new active version while retaining prior verification versions through the throttle window, restart API, then remove expired versions.
secrets.recovery: Recover the versioned keyset from the deployment secret store before serving authentication traffic.

secrets.name: AUTH_SIGN_IN_DEVICE_KEYSET
secrets.rotation: Add a new active version while retaining prior versions for the thirty-day device-token lifetime, restart API, then remove expired versions; never reuse a throttle-subject key.
secrets.recovery: Recover the versioned keyset from the deployment secret store; losing it only returns browsers to the per-account sign-in ceiling.

secrets.name: INTEGRATIONS_ENCRYPTION_KEYSET
secrets.rotation: When DAV is enabled, add a new active key while retaining old decrypt keys, restart API, re-save provider secrets, then retire unused keys.
secrets.recovery: Recover the complete keyset before restoring DAV subscriptions; otherwise keep DAV disabled.

secrets.name: GATEWAY_TLS_PRIVATE_KEY_PATH
secrets.rotation: Install the replacement certificate and key through the deployment secret mount, reload gateway, verify HTTPS, then remove the old mount.
secrets.recovery: Reissue from the certificate authority; never copy the private key into application archives.

secrets.name: PRIVATE_PRODUCTION_ARCHIVE_KEY
secrets.rotation: Write new archives under the new external encryption key and retain old keys until every retained archive using them has expired.
secrets.recovery: Keep an independently recoverable key copy outside the host and verify access before every release.
